findings: Both full captures describe a synchronous documented path for businesses accepting only US and Canadian cards. The browser-hosted Elements iframe keeps card details from merchant code. Stripe.js creates a card PaymentMethod and the merchant server receives its ID, determines the amount, and creates and immediately confirms the PaymentIntent with confirm=true and error_on_requires_action=true. The server observes success or failure, so this path can handle immediate post-payment actions without a webhook. Global/other-method integrations handle authentication requests and recommend webhooks for post-payment tasks (old raw lines 8–35, 49–53, 71–104, 272–345; new raw lines 9–49, 63–67, 83–116, 290–325).

Stripe documents succeeded as the success status. In the authentication-required example the error code is authentication_required, the decline code is authentication_not_handled, and the Intent status is requires_payment_method. Preserve ordinary invalid card/funds failures separately. The new diagram omits those other failure branches; `no authentication required` is not evidence of unconditional success, and PaymentMethod creation is not a completed payment. Both captures point to the global or upgrade integration to support bank-requested authentication (old raw lines 18–30 and 345–418; new raw lines 19–31, 35–44 and 321–394).

reviewed_answers.Q1: https://docs.stripe.com/payments/without-card-authentication documents a regional flow for businesses accepting only US and Canadian cards. At new raw lines 9–49, 83–116 and 290–325 the buyer enters card details into Stripe-hosted Elements, the browser creates a PaymentMethod and gives the merchant server its ID, and the server calculates the amount and immediately confirms a PaymentIntent using error_on_requires_action. Both captures require the HTML/JS script to load directly from js.stripe.com without bundling or self-hosting and the Elements page to use HTTPS in both client variants (old raw lines 35–53 and 148–152, new raw lines 49–67 and 160–164). These conditions describe the documented integration, not a merchant PCI conclusion. A succeeded result supports immediate post-payment handling without a webhook in this synchronous path. A required bank authentication fails this path with the authentication_required error, authentication_not_handled decline code and requires_payment_method in the example (new raw lines 351–376). May documents the same outcome with an Express handler (old raw lines 8–35, 272–345 and 375–400). source-stripe-payments-without-auth.md captures the basic flow but should preserve the server price decision, explicit success check and scoped webhook wording.
reviewed_answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/without-card-authentication, the November changes include an explanatory text diagram and React link selectors, a versioned Stripe.js include changing Dahlia to Endive (old raw lines 39–45; new raw lines 53–59), and Ruby SDK installation with a cURL request replacing May's Node/Express sample (old raw lines 261–345; new raw lines 274–321). These are presentation, navigation and implementation-example changes, with the same documented payment behavior in both. Preserve the May and November provenance and reciprocal stripe-payment-intents route in source-stripe-payments-without-auth.md. Keep only US/Canadian cards, immediate actions without webhooks within this synchronous path, the global webhook recommendation and the distinction between success, normal decline and authentication-required failure (old raw lines 8–30 and 375–418, new raw lines 9–31 and 351–394). The diagram is a simplified branch, not a promise that lack of authentication ensures payment success. Scope the reciprocal concept’s ‘no webhooks’ wording to these immediate actions and keep the global recommendation distinct. The term ‘legacy’ in the summary and concept does not establish deprecation.
